main_text.p: lementis, de rebus miftis; &c. An potius distinctæ sint disciplinæ vocandæ; ut Arithmetica, Geometria, aliæque Mathematicæ disciplinæ distinguuntur, in dubio positum est: & licet pro utraque parte rationes sint non contemnendæ, nos tamen eam partem sequimur, quæ partes quidem in Metaphysica admittit ut in Physica; scientiarum multitudinem non item. Scientiæ enim non sunt multiplicandæ secundum genera & species (aliâs namque Physica constaret tot scientiis quot partibus, alia esset scientia quæ de Corpore loqueretur, alia quæ de Cœlo, alia quæ de Elementis) sed secundum modum considerandi: atqui modus considerandi in Metaphysica unus & idem est, quicquid enim illa considerat, debet à materia sejunctum esse.

XII. Hactenus de Objecto. Genus Metaphysicæ est Scientia, idque stricta ratione, qua scientia ab arte & prudentia distinguitur. Ars enim non est, quia non est posita in ποιήσει[?], nec versatur περὶ γένεσιν τὴν τέχνας[?] ... ἀλλὰ τῆς θεωρεῖν, ὅπως ἂν γένηταί τι τῶν ἐνδεχομένων, τὸ εἶναι, τὸ μὴ εἶναι[?]. Non etiam Prudentia, quia non deliberat περὶ τὰ ἀγαθὰ[?] τῆς πρακτικῆς, nec docet quid eligendum vel fugiendum sit. Adhæc Metaphysica habet ea omnia, quæ scientia strictè dicta requirit: habet enim subjectum θεωρη-τόν[?], habet affectiones proprias, habet principia tùm complexa, tùm incomplexa, qui-

page.notes: The Greek passages are only partly legible at this scan resolution. The words marked [?] are best readings, and the stretch between "ποιήσει" and "ἀλλὰ" is not read reliably, so it is shown with an ellipsis-like gap. The phrase "nec versatur" is followed by Greek that could not be fully copied. The word "miftis" is as printed. The catchword "bus" is at the foot and is not repeated in the text; the paragraph ends on the hyphenated "qui-" because the next page continues the word. The faint digitiser mark at the lower right was omitted.
